meta.subtitle: Chinaimo WTP-style illustrative technical assessment
meta.dataBoundary: Public project scope informed the mock WBS. Quantities, rates, durations, logic, progress, claims and delay scenarios are illustrative assessment data and are not Kubota Construction contract data.

scenarios.name: Critical Activity Delay
scenarios.result: Project completion moves by 10 working days.
scenarios.why: Native Microsoft Project recalculation confirms that the delayed filter-structure activity remains on the controlling path and the added duration propagates through downstream process installation and commissioning.
scenarios.planningResponse: Protect the filter-to-process-piping interface, test permissible overlap/resequencing of downstream preparation, review resource acceleration options, and monitor the controlling chain at each update. Any recovery commitment should be supported by a recalculated programme rather than an assumed offset.
scenarios.residualRisk: Completion remains exposed until recovery on the controlling path is demonstrated in the updated schedule.

scenarios.name: Non-Critical Delay
scenarios.why: Native Microsoft Project recalculation shows the delay remains within available float / parallel-path flexibility and does not control the completion milestone.
scenarios.planningResponse: Record and monitor the consumed float, protect interfaces with building finishes/MEP and avoid allowing repeated slippage to convert the path into a near-critical constraint.
scenarios.residualRisk: No current completion impact, but remaining float should be tracked rather than treated as free time.

scenarios.name: Multiple Concurrent Delays
scenarios.result: 25 reported delay-days do not equal 25 project-delay days; net completion impact is 10 working days.
scenarios.why: The controlling-path delay governs the forecast finish while the concurrent building delay remains within its parallel-path float. Delay events therefore cannot simply be added arithmetically.
scenarios.planningResponse: Manage each event on its own logic path, focus recovery effort on the controlling WTP/process chain, and separately monitor float erosion on the building path.
scenarios.residualRisk: A later change in logic, float consumption or interface dates can alter which path controls completion.

scenarios.name: Procurement Watch
scenarios.result: Float is consumed; completion remains unchanged in this test case.
scenarios.why: The procurement delay does not yet push the receiving-equipment requirement far enough to control energization or the downstream commissioning path in the native recalculation.
scenarios.planningResponse: Track required-on-site dates, approvals, manufacturing/shipping milestones and energization interfaces. Escalate before procurement float is exhausted rather than waiting for a critical-path conversion.
scenarios.residualRisk: Procurement can become critical rapidly if delivery slips into the energization or commissioning window.
